description: Editorial reference model for a complete agent. Product artifact — not a constant buried in code.

layers.name: Ingress
layers.question: How does a request reach this agent?
layers.whatFillsIt: HTTP routes, webhooks, WebSocket handlers, phone/voice adapters, or queue consumers that call into the agent.
layers.whyItMatters: Without a mapped ingress you cannot reason about who can invoke the agent or how identity arrives.

layers.name: Context
layers.question: What prompt and configuration are assembled per turn?
layers.whatFillsIt: System prompts, prompt templates, per-turn config, and session context builders.
layers.whyItMatters: Context is the policy surface — what the model is allowed to know and how it is instructed.

layers.name: Reasoning
layers.question: Which model, provider, and control loop run the agent?
layers.whatFillsIt: Model client construction, provider/SDK, and the tool-loop or hosted control flow.
layers.whyItMatters: Reasoning is the decision engine; provider and loop shape latency, cost, and failure modes.

layers.name: Tools
layers.question: What can the agent call?
layers.whatFillsIt: Tool declarations with handlers (or hosted tool bindings) reachable from the agent loop.
layers.whyItMatters: Tools are the blast radius — every sensitive reach starts here.

layers.name: Memory
layers.question: What survives a turn or a session?
layers.whatFillsIt: Session stores, conversation history, KV/meta tables, and agent state snapshots.
layers.whyItMatters: Memory decides whether patient or money data persists beyond a single reply.

layers.name: Knowledge
layers.question: What does the agent retrieve from outside the turn?
layers.whatFillsIt: Vector store clients (Pinecone, Weaviate, Chroma, Qdrant, pgvector) and embedding / RAG calls.
layers.whyItMatters: Retrieval can pull PHI or proprietary text into the prompt without an explicit tool name.

layers.name: Data
layers.question: Which stores do the tools reach?
layers.whatFillsIt: Databases, tables, and external APIs attributed from tool reach (patient, money, internal).
layers.whyItMatters: Data is the sensitivity map — Guard and Reach exist to make this layer honest.

layers.name: Safety
layers.question: What validates, moderates, or redacts model output?
layers.whatFillsIt: Moderation endpoints, guardrail libraries, and PII/PHI redaction on the agent path.
layers.whyItMatters: Without safety on this agent's path, sensitive tools can leak through unchecked model text. System-wide guardrails on other services do not fill this row.

layers.name: Observability
layers.question: Are model and tool calls on this agent path traced as first-class events?
layers.whatFillsIt: Tracing SDKs and logging that specifically records model calls or tool calls on this agent's path — not generic HTTP access logs, and not traces on a different service.
layers.whyItMatters: You cannot debug or audit an agent that only leaves request logs on its own path. Observability elsewhere in the system does not fill this row.

layers.name: Evaluation
layers.question: How is the agent scored before release?
layers.whatFillsIt: Eval harnesses, test sets, scoring scripts, and CI workflows that run agent evaluations.
layers.whyItMatters: Without evaluation, regressions in safety or tool use ship silently.

layers.name: Deployment
layers.question: Where does it run and how are secrets supplied?
layers.whatFillsIt: Runtime process entrypoints, env/secret references, and deploy configs that start the agent path.
layers.whyItMatters: Deployment is where keys leak and where the wrong model can be pointed at production data.
